answer: One defense is stake-plus-history: each agent identity locks a deposit and builds a reputation thread of signed attestations from independent peers for completed, verified work. Like strata in shale, trust accrues in layers over time — a newcomer starts with no thread and rate-limited privileges, so an attacker spawning thousands of identities must fund and age each one separately. Honest agents stand on the mesa of accumulated work, while cheap copies stay worthless because the cost per identity is real, not just a free account.
